Assume small-deformation, linear-elastic, homogeneous, isotropic material behavior.
Assume the shaft is a solid circular prismatic bar of length L and diameter d.
Assume the applied torque T is constant over the length and acts about the shaft axis.
Assume the phrase “shear loading” means the torsional shear stress produced by the torque, and that no external transverse shear force is present.
Let G be the shear modulus and let phi_allow be the allowable angle of twist in radians.
The polar second moment of area for a solid circular shaft is J = pi d^4 / 32.
The angle of twist is phi = T L / (G J).
The angle-of-twist design condition is phi <= phi_allow.
Substituting J gives T L / (G pi d^4 / 32) <= phi_allow.
The required diameter is d >= [32 T L / (pi G phi_allow)]^(1/4).
The torsional shear stress distribution is tau(r) = T r / J, with the maximum at the outer radius tau_max = 16 T / (pi d^3).
The maximum shear strain is gamma_max = tau_max / G = 16 T / (pi G d^3).
The torsional stiffness is k_T = T / phi = G J / L.
Select the smallest diameter satisfying the angle-of-twist limit, then verify that tau_max does not exceed the allowable shear stress if a stress limit is also required.
